original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Inside the existing F2[Q8] dirty-register model with positive i/j calls: the complete space of linear identities among active compressions X M Y of label-block monomials of degree at most three is exactly the 7-dimensional span of the coefficient equations; exactly four unitriangular shears of degree at most two satisfy X(I+h)Y=0 and no degree-at-most-three product of two of them does; every pair of their images meets on an exact one-role three-call word. Conjecture: the four images together span at least 2t, which would imply n>=3t for every mixed shape. The (4,1) minimum is not decided. No new alphabet and no new kappa.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a new alphabet escapes the three-register obstruction. This package stays inside the specified F2[Q8] model and addresses the method question behind PR #4378's open (4,1) length: whether the cyclic two-identity subspace proof of n>=3t has a mixed analogue. A scoped negative method result is retained without a supplier; no construction round is started.
bottleneck_link: Side result in the nonabelian register model. It does not change the selected conditional kappa, and no physical caller or supplier admission is claimed.
stop_rule: Stop once the degree-three identity space, the shear classification and the six pair witnesses are certified, and the four-image conjecture is recorded with its complete small censuses. Do not search 13-call (4,1) words.
evidence: PROOF.md, WITNESS.json and verify.py: exact endpoints of 25 witness words with compression rank 25 of 32; exhaustive check of 4095 strict block polynomials and 12 shear products; six one-role pair witnesses; complete meet-in-the-middle censuses (1 role length 3; 2 roles lengths 5-7, and 8 with --full) with the four-image span at least 2t on every mixed-label word; failure controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Is dim(K1 U + K2 U + Q1 U + Q2 U) >= 2t for every exact mixed positive-Q8 word?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It implies n>=3t for every mixed shape, so the minima at (4,1) and (7,1) would be 15 and 24.
open_questions.first_step: Test three-role length-9 words with t=3, then seek a filtration argument using K2=K1+(ij+ji) and Q2=Q1+(ij+ji).
open_questions.blocked_by: No proof; the census here only reaches t<=2.

open_questions.question: Which compression identities exist at degree four and higher?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Theorem A stops at degree three; a higher identity could restore a cyclic-style argument.
open_questions.first_step: Build two- and three-role witness sets and explain any rank deficiency before trusting a relation seen only on two-role samples.
open_questions.blocked_by: Two-role length-8 samples leave a 16-dimensional annihilator at degree five, which may be small-dimension artefacts.

open_questions.question: Does an exact 13-call word exist at shape (4,1)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would refute Conjecture D and give the first mixed saving below 3t.
open_questions.first_step: Restrict to six-role scalar cores (PR3536 half-call core bound) and search the surviving splits (4,9), (6,7), (8,5), (10,3).
open_questions.blocked_by: Search size far beyond the census here.
